newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse index eases, market in lull.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse index eases, market in lull.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share index eased marginally on Thursday at the end of a four-day week of lucklustre trading, bourse officials said.
The index lost 19.50 points to close at 3354.12. Turnover was posted at 11.041 million shillings on 293,246 shares compared to 22.153 million shillings on 407,566 shares.
"There really is no interest in the market at the moment now that most of the blue-chips have announced their results," a senior broker said.
"In fact, it will be quiet since there are no fresh factors," another broker said.
On average, prices of major shares eased marginally.
Kenya Commercial Bank eased to 94 from 96 while Standard Chartered Bank was unchanged at 46.75.
Sasini Tea & Coffee closed at 75 unchanged while Rea Vipingo was unchanged at 9.
"The Easter mood has set in, which may also be a reason for today's dull trading session," a bourse official said.
Total Kenya closed at 62 from 64 while British American Tobacco Kenya eased to 62 from 65.
For the last three weeks, there has been a lot of selling pressure at the Nairobi bourse with investors holding out on buys for lower prices.

Brokers said they expected the current lull in the market to continue, at least for the short term, in the absence of fresh factors at least until mid-year when there would be a surge in speculative buying ahead of half-year results.
Uchumi Supermarket closed at 36 from 35.25 while Kenya Airways traded at 8.35 from 8.25.
